We can also construct **[prediction intervals](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-prediction-interval)** for
the value of a new observation $Y^*$,
given a covariate pattern $\vxs$.

A new observation $Y^*$ at $\vxs$ follows the same linear model as the [training data](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-training-set):

$$Y^* = \tp{(\vxs)}\vb + \eps^*$$

where $\eps^* \sim \ndist{0, \sigma^2}$ is [independent](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/independence.html#def-indpt) of the training data
(and therefore independent of $\eb$).

The [predicted value](#def-predicted-value) of $Y^*$ is:

$$\hat{Y}^* \eqdef \hat\mu(\vxs) = \tp{(\vxs)}\eb$$

We base the prediction interval on the **[prediction error](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/prediction.html#def-prediction-error)** $Y^* - \hat{Y}^*$:

$$
\ba
Y^* - \hat{Y}^*
&= \tp{(\vxs)}\vb + \eps^* - \tp{(\vxs)}\eb
\\
&= \eps^* - \tp{(\vxs)}(\eb - \vb)
\ea
$$

Assuming the model is correctly specified, the predictions will be [unbiased](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-unbiased):

$$
\ba
\E{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}
&= \E{\eps^*} - \tp{(\vxs)}\E{\eb - \vb}
\\
&= 0 - \tp{(\vxs)} \cdot 0
\\
&= 0
\ea
$$

The [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance) of the prediction error is:

$$
\ba
\Var{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}
&= \Var{\eps^* - \tp{(\vxs)}(\eb - \vb)}
\\
&= \Var{\eps^*} + \Var{\tp{(\vxs)}\eb}
\quad \text{(since } \eps^* \ind \eb\text{)}
\\
&= \sigma^2 + \tp{(\vxs)}\Var{\eb}\vxs
\\
&= \sigma^2 + \tp{(\vxs)}\paren{\sigma^2(\mX'\mX)^{-1}}\vxs
\\
&= \sigma^2 + \sigma^2\tp{(\vxs)}(\mX'\mX)^{-1}\vxs
\\
&= \sigma^2\paren{1 + \tp{(\vxs)}(\mX'\mX)^{-1}\vxs}
\ea
$${#eq-prediction-var}

::: notes
See @hoggtanis2015 §7.6 (p. 340).
:::

The variance (@eq-prediction-var) has two components:

- $\Var{\eps^*} = \sigma^2$:
the variance of the future observation's own noise,
the residual variance, which is irreducible given $\vxs$.

- $\Var{\dprodf{\vxs}{\eb}} = \tp{(\vxs)}\Var{\eb}\vxs$:
the variance due to estimating the mean $\dprodf{\vxs}{\vb}$ from the data.

The first component is not present in the [confidence interval](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/inference.html#def-confidence-interval) for $\hat\mu(\vxs)$,
which only accounts for estimation uncertainty.
This extra variance component is why prediction intervals are always wider than the corresponding confidence intervals:
a prediction interval must additionally account for
the noise $\eps^*$ in a new observation.

The **[standard error](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/estimation.html#def-SE)** of the prediction error is the square root of its variance:

$$
\SE{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}
= \sqrt{\Var{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}}
= \sigma\sqrt{1 + \tp{(\vxs)}(\mX'\mX)^{-1}\vxs}
$$

Replacing $\sigma$ with the residual standard error $\es$ gives the estimated standard error:

$$
\HSE{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}
= \es\sqrt{1 + \tp{(\vxs)}(\mX'\mX)^{-1}\vxs}
$${#eq-prediction-se}

Since $\eps^* \sim \ndist{0, \sigma^2}$ and $\eb \sim \ndist{\vb, \sigma^2(\mX'\mX)^{-1}}$
are both normally distributed,
and since $\eps^* \ind \eb$ (by independence of the new error term and parameter estimates),
their difference $Y^* - \hat{Y}^* = \eps^* - \tp{(\vxs)}(\eb - \vb)$
is also normally distributed,
with mean 0 and variance given by @eq-prediction-var.
Standardizing by dividing by $\sigma\sqrt{1 + \tp{(\vxs)}(\mX'\mX)^{-1}\vxs}$
yields a [standard normal](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-std-normal) [random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-random-variable).
Replacing $\sigma$ with $\es$,
which is estimated with $n-p$ degrees of freedom and is independent of $Y^* - \hat{Y}^*$,
the standardized prediction error follows a $t$ distribution:

$$
\frac{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}{\HSE{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}} \sim t_{n-p}
$$

Therefore, a $(1-\alpha)$ **prediction interval** for $Y^*$ is:

$$
Y^* \in
\paren{
\hat{Y}^*
\pm
t_{n-p}\paren{1 - \frac{\alpha}{2}}
\cdot
\HSE{Y^* - \hat{Y}^*}
}
$${#eq-prediction-interval}

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
x <- tibble(age = 40, sex = "male")
bw_lm2 |>
  predict(newdata = x, interval = "predict")
```

---

If you don't specify `newdata`, you get a warning:

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
#| warning: true
bw_lm2 |>
  predict(interval = "predict") |>
  head()
```

The warning from the last command is: "predictions on current data refer to *future* responses" (since you already know what happened to the current data, and thus don't need to predict it).

See `?predict.lm` for more.
